title: Check yourself: MCP advanced: multi round-trip requests, elicitation, sampling and notifications

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Under the 2026-07-28 revision, a tool needs a person's answer halfway through a call. How does the server get it?

options.text: It sends the client its own request on an open stream and waits for the reply
options.says: Ruled out because "The previous pattern of server-initiated requests is no longer supported."

options.text: It pauses the call and holds the connection open until the client answers
options.says: Ruled out because the pattern works "without requiring a shared storage layer across server instances or requiring stateful load balancing", which a held connection would need.

options.text: It stores the question in a session, which the client resumes later
options.says: Ruled out because the pattern allows "servers to request additional information without maintaining any server-side state", so there is no session to resume.

options.text: It returns an input-required result, and the client repeats the request with the replies
options.says: The page says the server answers with an input-required result, and the client "then retries the original request including the additional requested information".

questions.stem: A client receives an opaque string called requestState together with an input-required result. What must it do with that string?

options.text: Send back the exact same value on the retry, without reading it
options.says: The page says "Clients MUST NOT inspect, parse, modify, or make any assumptions about its contents", and that the client must echo the exact value on the retry.

options.text: Discard it, since only the answers to the questions matter on the retry
options.says: Ruled out because "the client MUST echo back the exact value of that field when retrying the original request", and the retry needs it, since the server keeps nothing else.

options.text: Keep it in a cookie so that other calls running in parallel can reuse it
options.says: Ruled out because both fields "MUST NOT be used for any other request that the client may be sending in parallel".

options.text: Decode it to learn what the server wants, then adjust it before the retry
options.says: Ruled out because "Clients MUST NOT inspect, parse, modify, or make any assumptions about its contents."

questions.stem: A server must collect a payment card number from a user during a tool call. Which mode of elicitation may it use?

options.text: The form one, since the client validates every field against a schema
options.says: Ruled out because "Servers MUST NOT use form mode elicitation to request sensitive information", whatever the schema checks.

options.text: Either one, as long as the client shows the form to the person first
options.says: Ruled out because URL mode "keeps the data out of band so it never passes through the client or the LLM context", and a form always passes through the client.

options.text: The out-of-band one, where the person visits a separate web page
options.says: The page says "Servers MUST NOT use form mode elicitation to request sensitive information", and that such interactions belong in URL mode.

options.text: Neither one, since a server may never request data from a person
options.says: Ruled out because "Elicitation lets a server ask a person for more information", with URL mode for sensitive data.
